title: Container Info
description:
container-info, collateral-terms/v4: the document container-provisioned and container-retired events carry. Unlike every other event here it is authored by the ROUTER, not by an application: the provisioning engine materializes a container declared in the agreement's provisioningSpec and reports the account, policy, per-asset onboarding state and every provisioning step that failed.

A container is attested even when steps failed. What works is in assetFootprints (one per onboarded asset), what failed is in issues (each with its reason), and the registry entry the owner materializes reads DEGRADED (an issue, at least one asset onboarded) or ONBOARDING_FAILED (assets failed and none onboarded) instead of ACTIVE. A provisioning retry re-publishes the event at the same agreement version with a higher onboardingAttempt, and the latest event wins.

Being protocol-level, these events are exempt from the definition's event-vocabulary, emitter-role and payload checks; the container's effective provisioner role is a narrower authority drawn from provisioningSpec. A definition still declares the type so a transition can name it.

error.description: Reason a provisioning step failed, as the failing system reported it.

code.description: Error code; absent when none was reported.

caip19.description: CAIP-19 identity of an on-chain asset.

containerAccount.description: The account that IS the container.

profileId.description: Owner-profile resource carrying the container account at the provisioning org.

orgId.description: Organization holding custody of the container account.

policy.description: The account policy installed on the container, derived deterministically from the agreement id and container key.

version.description: Agreement version the policy was instantiated from.

assetFootprints.description: The container's per-asset network accounts: the wallets postings credit. One entry per onboarded asset; an asset still pending has none.

servesRoles.description: Agreement roles this container serves, copied from its declaration.

onboarding.description: Per-asset onboarding state, one entry per eligible asset. The event is published once every asset is onboarded or failed; the reason of a failed asset is its entry in issues.

onboardingAttempt.description: Provisioning attempt this event reports, 0 (absent) for the first. A retry re-runs the failed steps under the next attempt without an amendment.

issues.description: Every provisioning step that failed for the container, each with its reason. This is the list a provisioning retry re-runs, whether an operator or an application triggers it.

step.description: The provisioning step that failed. Open on purpose, so a new step is reported without a new bundle; readers must accept values they do not know. Current steps: asset-onboarding (the asset's network account could not be created), profile-share (the container profile could not be shared with a participant).

subject.description: What the step failed for: the asset id (the asset's CAIP-19 when it resolved to no asset) for asset-onboarding, the participant organization id for profile-share.

caip19.description: The failed asset, naming its network. Set for asset-onboarding only.

status.description: The step's outcome. Open on purpose, like step; currently always failed.

containerSpec.description: The authored container declaration this event materializes, embedded VERBATIM as protojson. The fold accepts the event only when this copy byte-equals the declaration carrying the same key in the currently consented agreement version: the copy-and-verify binding that stops a router inventing a container the parties never agreed to. Left unconstrained here because it is a protobuf projection, not a document of this schema's own.
